root_cause.text: NFS LOCALIO performed page-cache allocations on its backing file mappings without clearing __GFP_FS, allowing direct memory reclaim to recurse from the local backing filesystem back into NFS writeback (nfs_writepages) and deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds nfs_local_mapping_set_gfp_nofs_context() to clear __GFP_FS from the address_space gfp mask and invokes it before LOCALIO operations in nfs_local_iocb_alloc() and nfs_local_run_commit(), while the commit/CVE explicitly states this is to “prevent direct reclaim recursion back into NFS via nfs_writepages” and ensure “all its page cache allocations are done from GFP_NOFS context.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to clear __GFP_FS on NFS local mappings so page cache allocations use NOFS context and avoid reclaim recursion into NFS writeback.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, nfs_local_mapping_set_gfp_nofs_context(struct address_space *m), was added along with a comment explaining its purpose; the function reads the mapping's current GFP mask with mapping_gfp_mask(m) and updates it via mapping_set_gfp_mask(m, gfp_mask & ~__GFP_FS) to clear the __GFP_FS flag.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when this helper is used on an address_space, page cache allocations for that mapping will occur without filesystem reclaim permission, forcing GFP_NOFS-like behavior and preventing direct reclaim from recursing back into NFS writeback paths such as nfs_writepages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set NOFS allocation context on the file mapping during local NFS iocb allocation to prevent filesystem-reclaim-related issues in this I/O path.
intent_record.what: A call to nfs_local_mapping_set_gfp_nofs_context(file->f_mapping) was inserted in nfs_local_iocb_alloc() immediately before init_sync_kiocb(&iocb->kiocb, file).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this sets the file mapping into a GFP_NOFS allocation context before initializing the synchronous kiocb, causing subsequent memory allocations associated with this local NFS I/O path to avoid filesystem reclaim/reentrancy behavior that could otherwise lead to incorrect or unsafe execution under memory pressure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set GFP_NOFS context on the file mapping before local NFS commit fsync to guard against unsafe filesystem-memory-reclaim interactions.
intent_record.what: A new call to nfs_local_mapping_set_gfp_nofs_context(filp->f_mapping) was inserted in nfs_local_run_commit() immediately before the debug log and the vfs_fsync_range(filp, start, end, 0) call.
intent_record.how: This sets the file mapping into a GFP_NOFS allocation context before the commit fsync path runs, affecting memory-allocation behavior during local NFS commit processing and helping avoid filesystem reentry or reclaim-related issues while flushing the range.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure local NFS commit/fsync paths use a NOFS page-cache allocation context by configuring the file mapping to avoid filesystem reclaim recursion during writeback.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by clearing __GFP_FS / using GFP_NOFS on NFS local backing file mappings during commit/fsync, preventing filesystem reclaim from recursing into NFS writeback and deadlocking.

The change directly targets the root cause by applying a NOFS allocation context to the file mapping in the local NFS I/O path, preventing reclaim from entering filesystem writeback paths and thus addressing the deadlock caused by allocations without clearing __GFP_FS.

candidates.rationale: This commit/fsync path invoked writeback on the local backing file without first putting the mapping into a NOFS allocation context, allowing page-cache allocation reclaim to recurse into filesystem/NFS writeback and deadlock.

This local NFS I/O setup used the backing file for I/O without first configuring its mapping to clear __GFP_FS, so later page-cache allocations in this path could enter direct reclaim and recurse into NFS writeback.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fsync/commit path operated on the local backing file without first placing its mapping into a NOFS allocation context. As a result, page-cache allocations could retain __GFP_FS, enter direct reclaim, recurse into filesystem/NFS writeback, and deadlock.

This local NFS I/O setup initialized use of the backing file before configuring the file mapping for NOFS. That allowed later page-cache allocations in this I/O path to proceed with __GFP_FS set, enabling reclaim recursion back into NFS writeback and causing deadlock.

Author: Weston Andros Adamson <dros@primarydata.com>

    nfs: add LOCALIO support
    
    Add client support for bypassing NFS for localhost reads, writes, and

    nfs_local_probe() is stubbed out, later commits will enable client and

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the LOCALIO allocation paths used for read/write/commit and shows the GFP flags directly. The root cause is page-cache/backing-file allocations being performed without clearing __GFP_FS, which allows filesystem reclaim recursion into NFS writeback. In this code, the vulnerable construct is present in LOCALIO allocations: `nfs_do_local_read()` calls `nfs_local_iocb_alloc(hdr, localio, GFP_KERNEL);`, and `nfs_local_commit()` calls `nfs_local_fsync_ctx_alloc(data, localio, GFP_KERNEL);`. `GFP_KERNEL` includes `__GFP_FS`, so these paths do not prevent filesystem reclaim recursion. Although `nfs_do_local_write()` uses `GFP_NOIO` (`nfs_local_iocb_alloc(hdr, localio, GFP_NOIO);`), the file still contains other LOCALIO allocation paths using `GFP_KERNEL`, meaning the vulnerable construct exists in this commit. There is no visible fix here such as consistently using `memalloc_nofs_*`, `GFP_NOFS`, or otherwise masking off `__GFP_FS` around these backing-file/page-cache related operations. Therefore, this commit contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
